$schema-note: THE MEMBER LIST #601 ASKED FOR, as a committed artifact rather than a search.
A version-bearing literal is a hardcoded version string in PUBLISHED source.
The v0.1.2 release hand-corrected five of them and FOUR OF THE FIVE were
found by searching, not by enumeration. The failure mode is not carelessness:
a hand-maintained set has no member list anyone can check against.
`check-version-literals.mjs` compares this file against the tree in two
directions, and THE TWO ARE NOT THE SAME STRENGTH — the same asymmetry the
label-dependence registry states, for the same reason.
REGISTRY -> TREE is EXHAUSTIVE. Every entry here is checked: its file must
exist, the declared source line must still be present, and where the entry
names a canonical source the literal must equal it. This is the direction
that decays, because an entry nobody compares still READS as guarded.
TREE -> REGISTRY IS BEST-EFFORT. It fails on the undeclared literals it
finds and is SILENT on the ones it does not. Its reach is a regex for a
quoted `N.N.N` in non-test `.ts` files under `packages/*/src` — READ
`discoverLiterals` rather than trusting this sentence. Its known misses are
pinned as executable assertions in the self-test, so widening the pattern
reddens the assertion that says a shape is missed and forces this note to be
corrected in the same change.
IDENTITY IS THE SOURCE LINE, NEVER A LINE NUMBER. A number goes stale on the
next edit above it and nothing notices; the text is what the guard matches.
The mutation-audit ledger made the same choice for the same reason.
`mirrors` NAMES THE CANONICAL SOURCE, AND THE GUARD ONLY EVER COMPARES A
LITERAL TO THE SOURCE ITS OWN ENTRY NAMES. That is what makes the plugin/kit
exclusion structural rather than an omission: those entries name no manifest,
so there is NO PATH by which the guard could compare them to a package
version. Do not 'simplify' this by deriving every literal from package.json —
that was proposed, refuted from source, and withdrawn, because
docs/compatibility-policy.md states the plugin API carries its own
`apiVersion` which moves INDEPENDENTLY of the package version. Deriving them
would break a published compatibility guarantee.

literals.reason: The core package's own version, exported for consumers. Mirrors the manifest and must move with it.

A LITERAL BY DELIBERATE DECISION, and that decision survives: the built `dist/` is what `npx` runs, and resolving the manifest from there needs a path that differs between the source tree and the published tarball, so a constant the release bump touches alongside package.json cannot resolve to the wrong file. This guard is what makes 'the release bump touches both' checkable instead of remembered.
The server version the inspect command reports. Mirrors the cli package version.

The server version the HTTP transport advertises. THIS ONE WAS ON NOBODY'S LIST — it is absent from the enumeration #601 was scoped from, and it reads 0.1.2 today by luck rather than by anything checking. It is now a published surface: v0.1.2 shipped to npm with SLSA provenance attached.

THE PLUGIN API VERSION, NOT A PACKAGE VERSION. docs/compatibility-policy.md states the plugin API carries its own `apiVersion`, which moves INDEPENDENTLY of the package version. Comparing it to packages/core/package.json#version would break that published guarantee — and because `mirrors` is `none`, the guard has no path by which it could.

Inside a DOC COMMENT — an illustrative plugin manifest in the module's usage example, not executable code. Declared rather than skipped so the discovery pass has something to match; a literal that is merely ignored is indistinguishable from one nobody looked at.
A PLUGIN's own version, declared against the plugin API contract rather than the observability package version. Same independence as PLUGIN_API_VERSION.

The conformance kit's API version. NOTE THE COINCIDENCE, because it is a trap: packages/adapter-test/package.json is ALSO 1.0.0 today, so this reads like a manifest mirror and is not one. If the package version moves, this must NOT follow it — the kit version is a contract with consumers of the kit, not a restatement of the release number.

The MCP `clientInfo.version` the conformance bank presents to a server under test. It identifies the test client to the protocol, and is not this package's version — packages/adapter-conformance/package.json is 0.1.0, which is what makes that plain.

NOT A VERSION LITERAL AT ALL — an OpenAPI FORMAT default for a document that omits its `openapi` field. Declared rather than excluded by a hardcoded skip in the guard: an exclusion nobody can read is how a real literal eventually hides behind a pattern exception.
